teams.heading: Interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula recalls Caleb Muntz for Tokyo title decider
teams.body: Interim head coach Senirusi Seruvakula has recalled Caleb Muntz to start at fly-half for Saturday’s Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan. Muntz’s inclusion triggers a backline reshuffle, with Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula shifting to full-back and Tuidraki Samusamuvodre stepping in at inside centre. Fiji are chasing a third consecutive title after defeating the Brave Blossoms in the previous two finals. Seruvakula noted the hosts are “a well-coached side,” but insisted his side will prioritise their own strengths as they seek to improve their tournament record.

teams.heading: Sean Lynn leads Wales to emphatic eight-try victory over South Africa
teams.body: Wales secured a stunning 50-19 victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday, ending a nine-match winless streak in spectacular fashion. Co-captain Alex Callender was named player of the match, while tighthead prop Sisilia Tuipulotu scored two of the hosts’ eight tries. Head coach Sean Lynn hailed the performance as the start of a new DNA for the side, noting, "Those 23 players were aligned in everything, both sides of the ball, and they had that belief."

teams.heading: Eddie Jones backs experience as Japan prepares for Pacific Nations final
teams.body: Eddie Jones has prioritised "good experience and toughness" for today’s Pacific Nations Cup final against Fiji in Tokyo. Making two changes to the starting XV that defeated the USA, Jones has recalled Faulua Makisi at No.8, pushing Jack Cornelsen to lock. Tomoki Osada also enters the backline on the wing. Jones noted, "It’s our third final in a row so it’s a great opportunity for this team to grow," as Japan targets their first title since 2019.

teams.heading: Wales dominate South Africa in emphatic eight-try WXV Global Series victory
teams.body: South Africa suffered a heavy 50-19 defeat to Wales at Cardiff Arms Park in their WXV Global Series opener. Despite a try from Felicia Jacobs following a strong scrum, the visitors struggled to contain an inspired Welsh attack that secured six tries by half-time. South Africa’s discipline proved costly, with hooker Lindelwa Gwala sent to the sin bin during a difficult opening period. Tries from Tshiremba and Samboya were not enough to bridge the gap as Wales secured a commanding win.
